rationale_overall: This week's pool is dominated by noise that doesn't clear the swap bar: student/hobbyist robotics competitions, a uranium film festival, foreign military/drone conflict reporting (Russia-Ukraine, Iran, India-Pakistan arms deals, a Tejas crash), private-company or non-investable items (SpaceX Starship test flight, Holtec/Utah nuclear-hub MOU, China's state molten-salt reactor claim, Greenpeace uranium-shipment photo), and generic AI listicle click-bait. The substantive items this week reinforce existing holdings rather than surface a clearly stronger new vehicle: GOOGL got real catalysts (Gemini 3 launch, $40B Texas data-center buildout), NVDA got real catalysts ($15B Anthropic pledge with Microsoft, RIKEN quantum-AI supercomputer tie-up, and a Fool piece arguing NVDA itself is a levered way to play quantum upside), RKLB had a routine confidential-payload launch, and SMR had a minor 2% pullback with no thesis-relevant news. Quantum Computing Inc (QUBT) popped on an earnings beat, a legitimate quantum-wave data point, but a single volatile microcap earnings pop is not yet a 'clearly stronger' case for swapping out a core AI or nuclear/rockets holding, especially with NVDA itself flagged as capturing quantum upside. No swap justified this week; watchlist unchanged pending a stronger, corroborated catalyst.
